requirements.title: Add to Story entry is the plus badge on the viewer's own avatar
requirements.entry_point: Stories rail, own avatar, lower-right plus badge
requirements.behavior: The avatar body opens the viewer's own story if one exists; the plus badge opens Add to Story. The badge does not disappear once a story exists.
requirements.accessibility: visible badge is 18px but avatar and badge resolve as a single target of at least 44x44, the plus owning the lower-right quadrant

requirements.title: Three capture modes: one photo, front+back, library
requirements.behavior: Two camera modes of equal weight (Take one photo, Front + back) plus the library as a quieter third row. Front + back is a counted dual-shot: outward 1 of 2, selfie 2 of 2, each half independently retakable.
requirements.retention: nothing is captured on entry; nothing is shared until review
requirements.failure_recovery: camera permission denied offers the library fallback; capture failed returns to the shutter and never opens the review screen
requirements.accessibility: counted steps are labelled in words, not by position alone
exclusions: no crop or aspect-ratio selection step

requirements.title: Review-or-retake is a hard gate before anything is shared
requirements.behavior: The captured pair or single is a draft until accepted. Retake discards that shot and reopens the camera. Nothing has left the phone.
requirements.trust_boundary: nothing leaves the device before acceptance
requirements.retention: a discarded retake is not persisted
requirements.failure_recovery: the review-or-retake gate is unaffected by upload state
requirements.accessibility: the draft state is stated in words (Draft - not shared)

evidence.detail: e2e/add-story.spec.ts

requirements.title: Story compose carries exactly two metadata rows: Bar and People
requirements.behavior: Bar opens a search sheet over Compose (one bar at a time, current and recent) and returns. People opens a tag sheet over Compose (accepted friends only, multi-select) and returns. The venue is a decision, never a detection: an empty venue is a finished state and the post carries no bar tag.
requirements.trust_boundary: tagging requires an accepted friendship with the AUTHOR
requirements.failure_recovery: if the tag read fails, the tag list must not render as nobody tagged
requirements.accessibility: sheets are 44px rows; caption is optional and length-labelled
exclusions: venue is never inferred from location
no caption form or settings stack in Compose

requirements.title: Story audience is chosen at action time from exactly three options
requirements.entry_point: Story audience subrow, directly above the publishing button
requirements.behavior: The audience is pre-filled from the Account default and offers Friends (all accepted friends), Selected groups, and Custom (pick people and groups). Changing it is a single-post override that never rewrites the Account default.
requirements.trust_boundary: server-enforced; a recipient outside the audience must not be able to read the story
requirements.retention: the audience selection lives as long as the story
requirements.failure_recovery: a failed audience write must fail the publish, not silently narrow or widen the audience
requirements.accessibility: the resolved audience is restated in words before publishing
exclusions: no Public option exists in any approved canvas

evidence.detail: Selected groups option depends on named groups, which do not exist; RLS never executed against staging

requirements.title: A story is visible for 24 hours
requirements.behavior: A story disappears 24 hours after capture. The publish summary states the exact expiry before publishing.
requirements.retention: 24 hours, unless also saved to the author's Night Out recap
requirements.failure_recovery: a skewed device clock must not hide media the database still serves
requirements.accessibility: expiry is stated in words, not implied by a fading affordance

evidence.detail: round-2 panel HIGH: a fast device clock gates media - ttl <= 0 yields mediaState expired and no URL

requirements.title: Stories are not public; viewing another person's story requires mutual friendship
requirements.behavior: A story is readable only by its author and by the members of its audience, and only where a mutual friendship exists.
requirements.audience: mutual friends within the selected audience
requirements.trust_boundary: row-level security in the database, not a client filter
requirements.failure_recovery: fail closed - an unresolvable friendship check denies the read
exclusions: no anonymous or bearer-link story access

evidence.detail: storiesRls.live.test.ts has NEVER EXECUTED - never passed, never failed, never forced green. The authorization claim is asserted, not proven. OA-01/OA-02 now permit staging evidence.

requirements.title: Story viewer chrome is the approved top metadata strip (Option A)
requirements.entry_point: tapping a story in the rail
requirements.behavior: Top chrome carries only progress, author, timestamp and close. Directly beneath the author row sit a venue chip and a people chip. Metadata never enters the system status area and never crosses a face.
requirements.failure_recovery: an inset-only signing failure must render the honest message, not a decorative glyph
requirements.accessibility: every tappable target is 44px or larger; content stays inside the safe areas
exclusions: Option B in-photo stickers and Option C bottom panel are not approved

evidence.detail: round-2 panel HIGH at StoryFrame.tsx:41 - the inset Surface is not passed photo.state

requirements.title: The people chip collapses to 'With <name> +N' and opens the tagged-people sheet
requirements.actor: audience member or a tagged person
requirements.entry_point: people chip, in-photo sticker, or bottom panel row
requirements.behavior: Any tag list longer than one name collapses to 'With Maya +2'. The sheet lists the full tag list, links each person to their profile, and offers Remove me to the viewer when the viewer is tagged. Automatic progression pauses while the sheet is open.
requirements.trust_boundary: removal is authorized to the tagged person only
requirements.data_owner: the tagged person owns their own tag
requirements.retention: a removed tag is gone from that story
requirements.failure_recovery: an unresolved first tag must not render a blank people chip
requirements.accessibility: every row is a 56px target
exclusions: no like counts appear on a story anywhere

requirements.title: The story queue advances automatically and returns to a documented surface
requirements.behavior: Progress segments equal the current person's item count. Items advance automatically; left and right tap zones move by hand. After the final item the viewer opens the next person who has an available story, in rail order, with no interstitial and no confirmation; author, avatar, venue chip, people chip and progress all change together. When the queue is exhausted the viewer closes and returns to Social - Tonight. X closes early and returns to the surface the viewer was opened from.
requirements.data_owner: each author owns their own items
requirements.failure_recovery: an unavailable person is skipped, not rendered blank
requirements.accessibility: a segment count is never shown without its meaning; there is no fixed 4- or 5-segment chrome

evidence.detail: e2e/story-rail.spec.ts

requirements.title: Automatic progression pauses for long-press, replies and accessibility focus
requirements.behavior: Progression pauses on long-press, while a reply is being composed, and whenever accessibility focus is on the chrome. It resumes only when that interaction ends.
requirements.accessibility: REQUIRED - a keyboard or screen-reader user must not lose a story to an auto-advance while reading its chrome

evidence.detail: round-2 panel MEDIUM: timer/long-press pause remains uncovered; the spec header now says so honestly rather than claiming coverage

requirements.title: A story ring means unseen; a pin badge means shared bar presence; they never merge
requirements.entry_point: Stories rail and Tonight presence rows
requirements.behavior: A ring around an avatar means an unseen story. A squared map-pin badge means shared bar presence. They are separate signals and are never merged into one affordance.
requirements.data_owner: each user owns their own story and pin state
requirements.accessibility: shape carries the meaning, not color alone
exclusions: the owner's ring must not represent story existence instead of unseen state

evidence.detail: round-2 panel MEDIUM: the owner's ring represents story existence rather than unseen state

requirements.title: The shared receipt restates the destination and audience and offers Undo
requirements.behavior: A concise confirmation with two actions and an X exit. It restates each destination with an indicator, the audience and the lifetime, and offers View story and Undo. The avatar keeps its plus so adding another moment stays available.
requirements.trust_boundary: Undo is authorized to the author only
requirements.retention: Undo removes the post and its bytes
requirements.failure_recovery: after the publish RPC is issued, a later throw must not delete bytes and report that nothing was shared
requirements.accessibility: two actions only; the X is the exit on every full-screen state

evidence.detail: publish ambiguity closed and verified by the round-2 panel: rpcIssued is placed correctly

requirements.title: Story media is venue-tagged and never geotagged; location metadata is stripped server-side
requirements.actor: the author, and any attacker running a modified client
requirements.behavior: Uploaded image bytes are re-encoded server-side so EXIF and GPS metadata cannot survive, and the content type is verified by inspection rather than by an allowlist of client-declared MIME strings.
requirements.audience: everyone who can read the story
requirements.trust_boundary: SERVER. A client-side strip is bypassable by definition and cannot satisfy this requirement.
requirements.retention: the original, unstripped bytes are never persisted
requirements.failure_recovery: a failed re-encode rejects the upload; it never falls back to storing the original
requirements.blocked_on: capability: server-side media ingestion boundary (sharp is already a dependency)

evidence.detail: CRITICAL, confirmed by both reviewer families: uploads go client -> Storage directly (stories.server.ts:254-266, 0065_stories.sql:51-61). Held rather than attested.

requirements.title: Signed media URL lifetime is enforced by the server
requirements.actor: the author, and any attacker running a modified client
requirements.behavior: The expiry of a signed media URL is decided and enforced server-side. A minted URL must not outlive the story's expiry or survive its deletion.
requirements.trust_boundary: SERVER. A client-side clamp on expiresIn is not enforcement.
requirements.retention: a URL's validity never exceeds the story's remaining lifetime
requirements.failure_recovery: a signing failure renders the honest media state, never a decorative placeholder

evidence.detail: CRITICAL, confirmed by both families: signedUrlTtlSeconds is a client-side clamp (stories.server.ts:38-47, 158-173, 433-441); createSignedUrl accepts any expiresIn from an authorized modified client

requirements.title: Deleting a story removes its bytes and its audience and tag metadata
requirements.behavior: Deletion removes the stored bytes and makes audience and tag metadata unqueryable. Media still referenced by another live story is never destroyed.
requirements.trust_boundary: prefix-scoped removal cannot touch another user's bytes
requirements.retention: no residual bytes and no residual metadata
requirements.failure_recovery: when the pre-read returns no row, the RPC-returned paths are reported as orphans rather than reporting success over zero rows

evidence.detail: round-2 panel: deletion unbroken and verified, but three HIGHs remain open - cross-story media destruction (introduced by the same fix), the expiry-race silent orphan, and audience/tag metadata still queryable after expiry (0065 'parties read')
